memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now Isaac had come from Beer Lahai Roi, for he was living in the Negev. He went out to the field one evening to meditate, and as he looked up, he saw camels approaching." - Gen 24:62-63 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
While Rebekah journeys toward him, Isaac is doing something beautiful: he goes out to the field in the evening to meditate. Before he meets his bride, we find him quietly alone with God. Here is a man whose habit is reflection and prayer.

The name of the place he came from — Beer Lahai Roi — means "the well of the Living One who sees me." Isaac had grown up near a place that testified that God sees. Now, in a peaceful evening, he steps away from the noise to be still.

In our busy, noisy lives, this simple picture is a gentle invitation. When did you last go out to the field, so to speak — set aside distractions and simply be present with God? Isaac's evening walk reminds us that a quiet, unhurried time with the Lord steadies the soul.

Notice too the timing. As Isaac lifts his eyes from meditation, he sees the camels approaching — God's answer arriving. Often it is in the quiet places, when we have made room for God, that we are best prepared to receive what He is bringing. Make space to be still, and lift your eyes; God may be nearer than you think.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When did I last set aside distractions to be still with God?
2. How could I build a quiet rhythm of reflection into my day?
3. Am I lifting my eyes to see what God is bringing?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, teach me to step away from the noise and be still with You. Steady my soul in quiet moments, and help me lift my eyes to see Your hand. Amen.
